x: The handicap was won by Mick Hamlin (3.45) a youngster with plenty of potential with veteran Dennis Logan (5:25) second and Steve (2.30) third.

Three new names are appearing regularly in recent results---Bob Picton (20) Mike Hamlin (20) and Chas Capener (19). Jack Goswell is enthusiastic about their potential and considers that with Gerry Cameron (still only 20) we have a quartet worth watching.

In the 'D' section Mick Hamlin and Bob Picton two of our young members who are showing plenty of improvement won their 6 mile badges. In section 'C' we saw some fine walking from Steve Laker-Jones when he finished 2nd and covered 7mls 196yds thus winning his 7 mile Badge.

Knifton and Laker-Jones were not in the best of form this time and Belgrave had to be content with 3rd place in the team event. Our most improved performer was undoubtedly Mike Hamlin who is moving steadily up the results.

Ray Middleton (54.25) was 4th, Mick Hamlin (58.36) was 13th, John Knifton, our only other starter, did not finish. Weather conditions made the track unsuitable and the race was held over the road circuit.
Mike Hamlin has moved from North-East London to Battersea and is ideally placed for full participation in race-walking, but we have not yet had the benefit of his support.
Turn-outs have been disappointing this summer and some faces rarely seen Steve Laker-Jones, David Mayo and Mick Hamlin for instance. We understand the latter is shortly going abroad.
He recently finished second in a road race, beating Mick Hamlin and Chris Henty in the process. There are other expatriates on the athletics scene out there "so it is not exactly lonely".
